articles.headline: Mike Tomlin reportedly has one major reason to stay away from NFL return
keyFacts: Former Pittsburgh Steelers coach Mike Tomlin is reportedly not guaranteed to return to NFL coaching in 2027.
Front Office Sports reported that Tomlin is enjoying his current, more relaxed broadcasting role with NBC as a studio analyst.
Tomlin has given no public indication of returning to coaching, though potential contractual complications with Pittsburgh also exist.
body: Photo by Joe Sargent/Getty Images Mike Tomlin is reportedly not guaranteed to return to NFL coaching in 2027 despite being expected to attract significant interest from teams looking for a new head coach.
The former Pittsburgh Steelers coach has made a strong start to his broadcasting career with NBC after stepping away from the sidelines following 19 seasons in charge of the franchise.
However, a return to coaching would mean giving up a role that offers him a more relaxed schedule and considerably less pressure than the demands of leading an NFL team.
Mike Tomlin’s new NBC role could keep him away from NFL coaching
According to Front Office Sports , Tomlin is enjoying his work as a studio analyst and is not necessarily prepared to leave it behind for another coaching opportunity.

One source told the publication: “Money has nothing to do with this. … Of course [NFL teams] are going to offer him stuff. The question is: Is he having a good time doing what he’s doing and is he good at it?”
Tomlin has quickly established himself as a popular voice on NBC’s Sunday Night Football coverage, with his direct opinions and trademark expressions attracting attention.
He has also started a YouTube channel to share his interest in Minecraft, giving him more time to pursue interests outside football.
That is a significant change from his previous role with the Steelers, where he never recorded a losing season across 19 years as head coach.

Tomlin led Pittsburgh to the playoffs 13 times and reached the Super Bowl twice, winning the championship once. His experience and record mean he is expected to rank among the leading candidates if teams make coaching changes.

The New York Jets and Washington Commanders have emerged as potential destinations in the speculation surrounding his future. However, both situations could require him to take charge of teams facing significant challenges.
There is also a potential contractual complication. Tomlin signed an extension with Pittsburgh through the 2027 season, although it is unclear whether the team has exercised its option for that year.
The Steelers could therefore retain contractual rights that might require another franchise to compensate them if it wanted to hire him.

For now, Tomlin has given no public indication that he intends to return to coaching. With his broadcasting career already gathering momentum, NFL teams may need to offer more than an attractive salary to convince him to leave the studio.

articles.headline: Karl-Anthony Towns gives 76ers props for second win over Knicks
keyFacts: New York Knicks All-Star Karl-Anthony Towns commended the Philadelphia 76ers for their 98-93 win in an NBA Cup matchup on Friday.
Towns stated that his team must learn from their pair of losses to the 76ers after dropping two matchups in 10 days.
The 76ers secured the five-point win after a 9-1 run in the final 90 seconds, capped by LeBron James' late layup.
body: Brad Penner-Imagn Images Karl-Anthony Towns gives 76ers props for second win over Knicks appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here .

New York Knicks All-Star Karl-Anthony Towns commended the shorthanded Philadelphia 76ers for their 98-93 win without All-Star Jaylen Brown in their NBA Cup matchup on Friday. Tyrese Maxey led with 27 points, and Anfernee Simons led the bench with 21 points for the 76ers. Jalen Brunson led the Knicks with 24 points, six assists, five rebounds, and two steals. Towns added 22 points, 12 rebounds, and three assists, but it wasn’t enough as New York came up short down the stretch.
After losing to the Knicks for the second time in 10 days, Towns stressed how his team has to learn from their pair of losses to the 76ers, per SNY Knicks.

“They’re a great team. Obviously, you have arguably the greatest player of all time. We’ve got to bring our best. We’ve got to execute at a high level. And we’ve got to continue to use these games as a learning experience.”

The 76ers went on a 9-1 run in the final 90 seconds to close out the five-point win. VJ Edgecombe’s three with 33.6 seconds left made it a two-possession game (94-90) before the Knicks failed to score a field goal in the final minute.

Brunson split a pair of free throws that could have made it a two-point game before LeBron James’ layup put the Sixers up for good with only 11.9 seconds left. James finished with 20 points on 8-for-15 shooting, including a pair of threes, nine rebounds, eight assists, one block, and one steal.

articles.headline: India news: Oil tanker carrying 27 Indians attacked with limpet mines in Strait of Hormuz
keyFacts: Limpet mines damaged the Panama-flagged oil tanker Louise 1 in the Strait of Hormuz, causing an engine room fire, maritime security sources said.
Indian Shipping Minister Sarbananda Sonowal said all 27 Indian crew members aboard the targeted oil tanker were safe and uninjured.
The UK Maritime Trade Operations reported that the ship's fire was extinguished and there was no environmental impact.
body: What you need to know
- The attack on the Panama-flagged Louise 1 occurred around 25 nautical miles (46 kilometers) northeast of Oman
- India's Shipping Minister Sarbananda Sonowal said all Indian seafarers aboard the vessel were safe and had sustained no injuries
Here are the top headlines from India on Saturday, October 31:
Strait of Hormuz attacks: Two tankers carrying Indians hit by mines in two days

An oil tanker carrying 27 Indian seafarers was targeted with limpet mines in the Strait of Hormuz.A small boat attached two mines to the vessel's hull, causing a fire in the engine room, maritime security sources said on Friday.

Indian Shipping Minister Sarbananda Sonowal said all Indian seafarers aboard the vessel were safe and had sustained no injuries. Sonowal also added that two Indians aboard another tanker that faced a separate attack on October 29 were also safe.
The attack on the Panama-flagged Louise 1 occurred on Thursday, around 25 nautical miles (46 km) northeast of Oman's Khasab.
The fire was extinguished, the crew was safe and there was no environmental impact, the UK Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) said.
The incident marks the first known successful use of limpet mines against a vessel in the waterway since the US-Iran war began in February.
The identity of those behind the attacks was not immediately known.

The Strait of Hormuz,a vital chokepoint for oil and gas transport, is seeing attacks on ships at the highest level since the Iran war began, according to US-based think tank Washington Institute for Near East Policy.

Incidentally, the Louise 1 was hit earlier with naval drones in the Black Sea by Ukrainian forces over its alleged role in transporting Russian oil and being part of the so-called shadow fleet of tankers deployed by Moscow.

articles.headline: US greenlights $2.1bn Patriot missile sale to Ukraine
keyFacts: The United States approved the possible sale of 500 Patriot PAC-3 missiles to Ukraine for an estimated $2.1bn.
Canada, Germany, Norway, and the European Union will help Ukraine fund the missile purchase to counter increasing Russian air strikes.
The missiles have yet to be made and delivery is not expected until the 2030s, people briefed on the decision said.
body: The United States says it has approved the possible sale of 500 Patriot PAC-3 missiles to Ukraine for an estimated $2.1bn.

The package of missiles, parts and support, announced on Friday by the US State Department, would be one of the most significant steps to supply defensive weapons to Kyiv since the start of the second administration of President Donald Trump in January 2025.
The Patriot system is the most effective weapon to counter fast-moving ballistic missiles.

Delayed missile deliveries, however, have stoked US-Ukraine tensions after Trump announced a diesel deal with Russia and criticised Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy for his unwillingness to stop attacks on Russian refineries.
Ukraine has long said it urgently needs more missile interceptors to knock down the growing waves of missiles Russia’s military fires at the country.

Zelenskyy said on Monday that Kyiv had been waiting for almost a month for Washington to sign off on critical missile supplies, as Russia stepped up its attacks on Ukrainian energy and civilian infrastructure.
A Russian drone strike on Thursday killed at least 14 people on a crowded rail platform in the Ukrainian city of Dnipro.
Five people were killed in daytime strikes on two other cities, and a late-evening missile strike killed one person in the capital, Kyiv, officials said.
Delivery years away
Despite Ukraine’s need for quick deliveries of the missiles, Kyiv is unlikely to receive the Patriot interceptors soon. Weapons sales typically take years to fulfil.
Two people briefed on the US decision said the missiles, which have yet to be made, are not expected to be delivered until a couple of years into the 2030s.

Ukraine will pay for the missiles with contributions from Canada, Germany and Norway through a programme called US JUMPSTART, along with national funds financed by the European Union’s Ukraine Support Loan, the State Department said in its statement.
US weapons manufacturer Lockheed Martin is the principal contractor for the sale of the Patriot interceptors.
The US Army awarded Lockheed a contract worth up to $58.6bn to produce Patriot interceptor missiles in July.

Lockheed has said the deal would allow it to follow through on a promise to triple PAC-3 production capacity by the end of 2030. It has previously announced that Patriot PAC-3 missile interceptor production would reach 2,000 units annually.
Pentagon negotiators are pressing weapons contractors to speed up production.

The US military’s supply of large quantities of weapons to allies and its own heavy munitions use for its operations in Iran have raised concerns about its inventories of key air defence and precision-guided weapons.

articles.headline: Pile-ins, payouts, and pacing pressure: the investors behind the VCs open up
keyFacts: Venture capital limited partners are experiencing high returns and concentration as funds heavily back OpenAI and Anthropic.
LPs note that accelerated fund-raising cycles and faster investment pacing present a yellow light and potential risk.
Industry executives Beezer Clarkson and Amit Bhatti stated that secondary markets and liquidity options have become more sophisticated.
body: The limited partners who provide the capital to venture firms — the “money behind the money” — are feeling great right now. They’re in uncharted territory in many ways, but also potentially exceedingly lucrative territory.

Normally, LPs typically spread their bets across many firms to diversify their own portfolios. They write checks to emerging managers and established ones, to generalist firms and specialists. The goal is a strong return, but also to minimize risk.

That’s the typical playbook. But typical is out the window. OpenAI and Anthropic’s valuations have shot up so quickly that nearly everyone has piled into the same two companies on the way up, often inside the same venture firm, despite the longstanding venture convention of avoiding investments that conflict with one another. No one is complaining, either. The LPs I speak with seem unbothered by this big gamble, given the potential returns; they’re expecting a bonanza.
But they do see danger ahead, even if they describe this as a “yellow light” situation, and they’re uneasy about how quickly VCs are coming back to raise new funds.

I talked about all of it recently with Beezer Clarkson of LGT Capital Partners, a Zurich-based diversified asset manager, and Amit Bhatti of TrueBridge, a Chapel Hill firm that focuses solely on venture. This conversation has been edited for length.
These are strange days — exciting but also scary. How are you feeling about your roles right now, and your place in this startup ecosystem?

Beezer Clarkson: It’s very busy, but I wouldn’t say it’s scary. There’s a lot of change and a lot of variables at play. I love venture, so I find the chaos fun. I’ve been doing this for a couple of decades, so seeing the cycles makes it less scary. You appreciate that these things happen, and that we should enjoy the upside, because sometimes there’s downside, and the up is a lot more fun than the down.

Amit Bhatti: If anything, it’s exciting. Venture is sometimes looked at as a niche, and now that AI is all-consuming, all the attention is on venture. This feels like our moment more than it is like, “Oh gosh, what’s going to happen?” The pace of investing and the valuations may be different, but really meaningful stuff is happening, and all the attention is focused on this corner of private equity.

Your funds all hold the same brands now, OpenAI and Anthropic, multiplied across however many funds you back, and your job is to keep your institutions diversified. How do you think about that? Obviously it’s great right now, but if things turned, it would be less great.

Amit Bhatti: Venture has always been a power law business, so I actually view the concentration as a good thing. If we were getting to the maturity of one of our funds and there were still lots of tiny positions, something’s gone wrong. Our funds that are 10-plus years old are starting to consolidate into a few names. There’s a lot of Databricks, a lot of SpaceX, a lot of Stripe. In this generation of funds, I would hope there’s a lot of Anthropic and a lot of OpenAI. That’s a feature, not a bug. Not every one of these companies is going to work out, but that consolidation is typical. What’s different is how quickly it’s happened. I don’t view it as an immediate panic signal.

Beezer Clarkson: At the early stage, you still see quite a diversity of opportunity sets, and the dollars are smaller. It aggregates up into the same companies, but early-stage funds obviously aren’t doing the big late-stage stuff, so you have more diversity there, if that’s what you’re looking for.
Funds that invested on four-year cycles have shrunk that to three, then two, then 18 months. Is the pacing okay, or is it concerning?

Beezer Clarkson: We’re seeing funds come back on one-year pacing, which is fast. The norm was probably two to two and a half years. Some funds are deploying much faster because they’re taking concentrated, big-check positions. That could be a worrisome sign. It could work out, we don’t know, but it’s typically harder to do a one-year vintage and get it right.

Amit Bhatti: Similar for us. I would have said 24 to 36 months was roughly normal. Now 12 to 18 is not crazy for some of the funds going really quickly. A lot of funds are bumping up their fund sizes mid-cycle, which is definitely unusual. That’s partly because rounds have gotten so large. If Anthropic is raising a giant quantum of capital and you put 20% of the fund into it, you’re obviously going to be ahead of pace. Seed round sizes have gone up almost 2x, too, so if you want to lead, you’re writing 2x the check. It’s definitely a yellow light. It gives us a little bit of heartburn.

But when we look at what these managers actually bought, the numbers are different. The last time we had accelerated pacing, there was a lot of investing in zero-revenue crypto moonshots. Now we’re seeing a lot of companies go from zero to $100 million in revenue, which was totally unheard of before.
If you’ve got a great manager who comes back every year but the returns are still on paper, can you say “call me next time,” or do you lose your seat at the table?

Beezer Clarkson: It’s very hard to leave a manager and then come back. It happens, but it’s more typical to downsize your check. In 2021, a lot of LPs said, “If I was going to give you $10 million, I’ll do $5 million, because $10 million was for two years.” In our portfolios, the pacing gets pulled through, so we think about our pacing as well as yours.

Amit Bhatti: Same here. We’re building out a calendar of when we expect to make commitments, so if someone goes way off that map, we need to make sure the capital is there. You see people downsize or communicate it up front. It’s hard to say you’re sitting it out altogether, because then you’re not reliable capital. That’s also why you’re seeing upsizes; managers don’t want to come back and say they’re raising a whole new fund, so they bump up the old one.

Beezer Clarkson: People also rotate out of venture sometimes because capital calls keep running with no distributions coming back, and they still have to meet operating commitments, whether it’s the endowment, the hospital, or the foundation. That puts a lot of strain on those situations.

LPs like time diversification, yet a lot of funds were raised in recent years, including that backed startups at high valuations during the pandemic. How are those funds doing, and how would you describe 2026 so far?

Beezer Clarkson: The 2021 vintages are still early, five years in, but they argue against doing one-year funds. Some will catch a piece of an AI company and look excellent, but your odds of getting it right in one year are just tougher, and the valuations were extreme.

Amit Bhatti: If I look at the last 15 years of our portfolio, I wouldn’t bet on the COVID vintage being the best one. But a couple of breakouts will come from it. OpenAI was around in that era, and Cursor started pretty far back, so they’re in some of those funds. And liquidity has started flowing. The past two years were definitely slower, but SpaceX is the headline, Cerebras was a big exit this year, there have been a couple of other IPOs, and a lot of M&A. We’re seeing $10 billion-plus M&A exits, a $60 billion one [with Cursor]. Liquidity is going beyond just IPOs.
How are your venture fund managers thinking about secondaries? If I were a VC, I’d have been tempted to take money off the table in OpenAI or Anthropic.

Beezer Clarkson: Secondaries have become much more sophisticated in venture over the last, call it, five years. It’s localized in the top handful of companies, but it’s much more prevalent than before, which I think is good, because the ecosystem needs liquidity options. Venture is predicated on that, and if you wait 20 years for an IPO, that is not what structurally we all thought it could be. They’re also happening at multiple levels now. LPs sell stakes of their GPs, a strip of their portfolio, and the taboo around it is less.

Amit Bhatti: It’s the third leg of liquidity now: IPOs, M&A, secondaries. Private equity has always had a well-developed secondaries market, and venture didn’t. It was kind of a dirty word. You were only selling if you were distressed. Then people were holding the bag in 2021 and thought, “I should have sold.” Now more managers use it as a tool, and more judiciously. If you still believe it’s the power law company, you’re probably not exiting the whole position. But if you can sell 20% of your position and return your fund, you should probably do it.
There’s a lot of founder selling and employee tenders — often very early into the company’s “journey.” How do you feel about that?

Amit Bhatti: We were talking before about the analogy to crypto, where things got very difficult in part because employees were paid in tokens that were liquid immediately. What’s your motivation to stick around when things get hard? So I think it’s great that there are employee tenders, especially for companies that have been around a long time, like Stripe and Databricks, with a very clear financial picture. For them to offer partial liquidity to employees is totally reasonable. But a lot of the enforcement falls on the lead investors. Investors we back have told companies, “We don’t want you to do an employee tender right now.” Those conversations are happening behind the scenes, and people have learned some lessons from last time. It’s all based on leverage, though. If the founder has incredible leverage . . .
Forget it.
Amit Bhatti: Yeah.
When these companies go public and employees get liquid, will they become partners or competitors to your venture managers? These employees have amazing networks.

Beezer Clarkson: We’ve seen it multiple times: when a company becomes very productive, employees can become LPs or GPs themselves. It’s entirely possible there’ll be a whole new raft of emerging managers backed by people coming out of OpenAI and Anthropic. It happened in the Google days. But being an LP means signing up for many millions of dollars and a multi-decade business.

Amit Bhatti: The real estate part [given the soaring cost of home prices in San Francisco] is going to be tough. But those people stay in the ecosystem, investing in others, building new companies, starting new firms. That’s why no other place is taking SF’s place anytime soon.
Housing costs here in San Francisco have shot up so fast. Do we price out the next generation of founders, and does the next hub end up in New York or somewhere else?

Beezer Clarkson: History would argue that the density effect in the Bay Area is a great pull. Maybe it moves out of San Francisco and back into the suburbs. Back in the day, YC was in Mountain View. New York obviously has its own very deep tech scene, but there’s such a density here that it’s been really hard to push back against.
A handful of venture funds now lock down most of the committed capital from limited partners. Is there a wedge in for emerging managers?

Beezer Clarkson: There are still first-time and emerging managers, funds one through three, being raised this year, last year, the year before. You still need a differentiated point of view, a reason for being. Fundraising has gotten harder, but we see them being funded, and the fund sizes are just smaller. Fifty percent of the money might go to the big funds, but if your average first fund is $25 million to $50 million, there can still be enough of those to add up to $1 billion.

Amit Bhatti: There are people raising $5 million or $10 million right here in SF, maybe formalizing their angel investing. A lot of really well-known funds started with a $5 million fund. It’s much better for an emerging manager to build the track record, prove out the thesis, your access and your judgment with whatever capital you have, and then fund two will be easier to raise. If you try to raise $50 million or $100 million on day one, you’re creating a giant hill to climb.
Beezer Clarkson: If you’ve only angel invested, that’s a different story from spinning out of a platform where you have an installed base of LPs who know you. Those managers typically raise more.
Can you talk about specific kinds of emerging managers you’ve backed, and what made you write the check?

Amit Bhatti: People define “emerging” very differently. We’ve backed founders who are still running their companies and investing on the side. We’ve backed people leaving a bigger firm for something earlier. And we’ve backed extremely young GPs, 22 and 23 years old, who have really close access to the next generation of AI-native founders. They started an accelerator program at MIT, Harvard, and Stanford, and the first couple of batches had Cursor and Mercor in them. They’re young, but they’re around an incredible density of talent. The VC job is sourcing, picking, winning, and they did a pretty decent job of picking when there was no money involved. Success begets success in venture, so we were happy to give them a shot.

Beezer Clarkson: There’s much more flexibility now. I remember a time when an LP wouldn’t fund somebody who had a job and was also investing, and people are open to that now. I’ve been investing in emerging managers, along with established ones, for 14 years, and they run the whole gamut, from an operator-turned-investor raising $10 million, to a spinout raising a few hundred million [dollars]. It’s interesting when they’re still operating, because it gives them insights. The trick is whether they’re doing what they need to do to win the right to be on the best cap tables.

Amit Bhatti: Especially early stage, there’s no one-size-fits-all. You can be part-time, you can be diversified, you can be concentrated. There are more outs in the deck, if you will, for returning something that’s small and experimental.
What’s the smallest check you’ll write to a fund, and how much of a fund will you take?

Beezer Clarkson: Given our program, it’s hard to do less than $5 million. I’ve generally taken the view that if you’re [representing] too much of a fund, there are challenges for the GP going forward, so I’d want to be no more than 20%. There are situations where I’d consider more.

Amit Bhatti: Three to five million for us, and on occasion smaller in very specific scenarios. We don’t really care about concentration if it’s the right scenario. We’ll do half or all of it. But Beezer’s right that it’s not ideal for the GP, and we tell them up front to diversify their LP base. We’ve done a fund where we were half the capital, and the next fund we were closer to 20%, because they did well.

articles.headline: 5 Must-Play New Xbox Games Coming in November, Including GTA 6
keyFacts: Polygon reported that November features multiple new Xbox releases alongside Grand Theft Auto 6, including indie titles and remasters.
The article listed Gravhounds launching on November 2, Escape Academy 2 on November 5, and Warhammer Survivors on November 10.
Shrek 2 Remastered launches on November 10, followed by Grand Theft Auto 6 on November 19.
body: If you only took a quick glance at November’s release date calendar, you might walk away with the idea that Xbox players are only getting one game this month: Grand Theft Auto 6. While that’s certainly the only big game coming to Series X, the first few weeks of November are deceptively crowded. A stack of indie hidden gems and nostalgic remasters are here to make sure you have something to play while you wait for your return to Vice City.

These are just five of the games you can look forward to in November. Yes, the list includes the big one, but there’s more to check out than you might think. If you’re not interested in going on an open-world crime spree, you’ll still have some solid options this month.
5 Gravhounds
Release date: Nov. 2

Though Xbox Game Pass isn’t getting any major tentpole releases in November, it is adding a lot of promising smaller games. Chief among them is Gravhounds, a new co-op shooter where you shoot aliens and build a base together. Sounds simple enough, but there’s one eye-catching twist: You play as a pack of humanoid dogs. Gravhounds has a real “WTF” factor that made it a standout game during this year’s Gamescom, so we’ll be curious to see if the shooting holds up to the wacky visuals.
4 Escape Academy 2: Back 2 School
Release date: Nov. 5

If you’re in the market for a great couch co-op game this month, don’t miss out on Escape Academy 2: Back 2 School. It’s an expanded sequel to 2023’s Escape Academy, a well-designed escape room game built for split-screen play. Back 2 School is building on its predecessor with more puzzle rooms, more fleshed-out worldbuilding, and even an explorable campus lined with secrets. If it’s even half as clever as the first game, it should be November’s best couples game.
3 Warhammer Survivors
Release date: Nov. 10

Do you like Warhammer? How about Vampire Survivors? If your answer to either of those questions is yes, you’ll want to check out Warhammer Survivors. The developers behind the very fun Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun are putting their knowledge of the tabletop universe to good use in a “bullet heaven” game full of carnage. Is it a bit of a gimmick? Maybe so, but you could say the same about Boltgun, and look how that turned out. Warhammer Survivors should offer plenty of reliable fun for fans of the auto-shooting action genre.
2 Shrek 2 Remastered
Release date: Nov. 10

Okay, it might look like Shrek 2 Remastered is only here as a gag, but hear me out. 2004’s Shrek 2 video game actually has some serious historical significance for Xbox: It was a major piece of Xbox’s E3 2004 presentation. In fact, it was the second game shown during the presentation, shown right after a short trailer for Unreal Championship 2: The Liandari Conflict. As weird as that seems, Xbox had a lot of faith in what turned out to be a pretty decent licensed game in an era where that wasn’t a given. The freshly remastered version brings history back to Xbox in the form of a nostalgic co-op adventure game.
1 Grand Theft Auto 6
Release date: Nov. 19

What else do I need to say here? Grand Theft Auto 6 is not only the main event of 2026, but likely of the decade at large. Rockstar’s open-world crime game promises to be a massive, boundary-pushing experience full of Florida flair. And despite the fact that so much about it has leaked, it still feels like we know next to nothing about the Bonnie and Clyde-inspired love story at the heart of it. That could stand to elevate a reliable bit of criminal chaos into something tender. We’ll find out together when the gates to Vice City finally open on Nov. 19.

articles.headline: By Skipping Last-Gen Systems, Stranger Than Heaven is Allowing RGG Studio to Fully Leverage the Power of Current-Gen Consoles at Long Last
keyFacts: Developer RGG Studio is building Stranger Than Heaven exclusively for current-generation hardware and PC, skipping previous-gen consoles like the PS4, according to producer Hiroyuki Sakamoto.
Sakamoto stated that avoiding hardware constraints allowed the team to display more characters on screen simultaneously and achieve higher character quality than past games.
Stranger Than Heaven is scheduled for release on PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X|S, and PC on January 15, 2027.
body: Stranger Than Heaven will apparently be the most technically accomplished game that developer RGG Studio has ever produced, and that’s largely due to the fact that it's being created solely for current generation hardware. The game’s producer, Hiroyuki Sakamoto, confirmed as much to IGN during an interview conducted at Gamescom Asia x Thailand Game Show 2026 this week.

“We set out to make Stranger Than Heaven as a completely brand-new game, with the goal of creating something entirely fresh while putting forth the absolute best quality we can produce right now,” explained Sakamoto. “[So] we decided to drop previous-gen platforms like the PS4 and focus on creating an experience best enjoyed natively on current-gen consoles like the PS5.”

Since the launch of the PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S systems back in 2020, all of RGG Studio’s games have still kept one foot stuck in the previous console generation. 2024’s Like a Dragon: Infinite Wealth was developed to run across two eras of PlayStation and Xbox, and while Xbox One was finally dropped for Yakuza Kiwami 3 & Dark Ties earlier this year, support for PlayStation 4 remained.

However, by developing Stranger Than Heaven purely for PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X|S, and PC, the team hasn’t had to make any hardware-based compromises to its vision for the new game’s multiple decade-spanning journey through early 20th century Japan.

“In the past, hardware constraints meant limiting the number of characters we could display on screen at once, among other things we had to give up on,” continued Sakamoto. “With Stranger Than Heaven, by fully leveraging the PS5's capabilities we were able to showcase more characters on screen simultaneously than ever before and raise character quality to the next level.”

Despite some lingering reservations regarding its digital resurrection of the late rapper Tupac Shakur, IGN's Michael Higham found a lot to like about Stranger Than Heaven in his recent hands-on preview . With just over two months to go before its scheduled release in January, Sakamato seems supremely confident in where the game is at, going on to state, “I think we succeeded in achieving our goal of creating a richer visual experience with a stronger artistic identity than anything we've done prior.”
During the same chat, Sakamoto also confirmed the inclusion of in-game “cheats” in Stranger Than Heaven that you can read about here .
Stranger Than Heaven is set for release on PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X|S and PC on January 15, 2027.

articles.headline: Verstappen, Lawson receive grid penalties after 'unacceptable' practice collision
keyFacts: Max Verstappen and Liam Lawson received one-place grid penalties for an unacceptable collision during practice at the Mexico City Grand Prix.
Stewards stated that both drivers behaved in an unacceptable manner and admitted the moves were unnecessary and clumsy.
Racing Bulls team principal Alan Permane said both drivers were at fault for the completely unnecessary collision.
body: Max Verstappen, Liam Lawson receive grid penalties for 'unacceptable' practice collision at Mexico City Grand Prix

Max Verstappen and Liam Lawson have both been handed a one-place grid penalty for their collision in second practice at the Mexico City Grand Prix; watch qualifying in Mexico at 9pm on Saturday and the race at 8pm on Sunday
Saturday 31 October 2026 03:12, UK
Max Verstappen and Liam Lawson have both received one-grid place penalties for an "unacceptable" collision in second practice at the Mexico City Grand Prix.

Verstappen tried to overtake Lawson up the inside at Turn 12 going into the old baseball stadium but the Racing Bulls driver held his ground, so the pair went side by side through Turn 13 and made contact at Turn 14 with a piece of debris falling off the Dutchman's car and causing a red flag.

Collisions of this nature between drivers in practice are extremely rare, and the stewards stated both drivers "behaved in a manner that was considered unacceptable" and that a warning had been given at the team managers meeting earlier on Friday about overtaking in the final sector.

The stewards also said that Verstappen and Lawson both admitted the moves were "unnecessary and clumsy".

They added: "Noting that there had been similar incidents this year of actions between drivers in Free Practice, the stewards have decided to escalate the penalty from that of a formal warning to a grid position penalty particularly in view of the warning that had been provided at the Team Managers meeting and consistent with other incidents involving contact between the cars in Free Practice in previous years."
'Not smart when you're fighting for your seat' - Verstappen hits out at Lawson
The incident was made even more surprising by the fact the two teams have the same owners, with Racing Bulls considered Red Bull's junior squad.

Racing Bulls have yet to confirm their 2027 driver line-up and Lawson's future is up in the air despite the New Zealander sitting ninth in the standings, 39 points ahead of his team-mate Arvid Lindblad and occupying the 'best of the rest' position behind the top four teams.
Asked about the incident before the stewards' verdict, Verstappen said: "I don't think it's called unlucky. Maybe not very smart behaviour what he was trying to do there.
"At the end of the day, it's not going to change my weekend.
"If I would be him, I would act a little bit smarter. Also, when you are fighting for your seat, it's not very smart behaviour."
Red Bull junior Nikola Tsolov, who made his F1 practice debut on Friday in Mexico, is second in the Formula 2 championship and remains in contention for a Racing Bulls seat next year.
Verstappen, who wields major power at Red Bull and over the summer signed a new long-term deal with the team, appeared to be referencing that situation with his comments.

In a separate interview, the four-time world champion added: "When he saw me coming, he suddenly started to accelerate. I don't know what was going through his head, that he wanted to drive me off the track in the hairpin.
"That's not very sensible behaviour from someone in his position, to pick a fight with me."
Lawson, who was Verstappen's team-mate for the first two rounds of the 2025 season before being brutally dropped by Red Bull, was not obliged to speak to the media after Friday's track action.

However, in the immediate aftermath of the incident, Lawson said on the radio that Verstappen "literally drove into me" and added "if I back out every single time, what the **** do I do? He actually came off the track into the side of me".
Racing Bulls team principal Alan Permane said both drivers were at fault for the "completely unnecessary" collision.
"I don't know what Max has said, I haven't heard or seen anything," Permane said.
"I'm sure he's got his opinion and Liam's got his opinion but mine is, it's just not needed and they can both do better."
Which driver was more in the wrong?
Three-time W Series champion and Sky Sports F1's Jamie Chadwick agreed with Verstappen's comments on the incident, given the situation he is in.

"If it's any other driver on the grid, you can stand your ground a little bit but when it's the senior team, the team that also have an influence on the decision that goes into your race seat, does he need to do that? Probably not," she said.

"But he was the same even when he raced Max as team-mates - he raced him very hard and they know exactly what that team is about, so I don't think that was the wisest thing from potentially either of them, but particularly Liam's side."
Former McLaren and Aston Martin strategist Bernie Collins says both drivers will "regret their decisions".
"Both drivers had an opportunity to do something different there and both drivers will think 'was that corner, really worth that?'," she said.
Is Lawson's seat under threat for 2027?
Lawson is the highest placed midfield driver in the F1 Drivers' Championship, with only the Mercedes, McLaren, Ferrari and Red Bull drivers ahead of him in the standings.

He has bounced back from a disappointing two races with Red Bull at the start of 2025 and did enough to be handed a full season at Racing Bulls this year, where he has outperformed rookie Arvid Lindblad.
Lawson has scored twice as many points as Lindblad and Sky Sports F1's Karun Chandhok thinks it would be "unjust" if Lawson lost his seat.

"He's done a fantastic job this season. He's come back carrying the mental baggage of being sacked from the Red Bull top team, went back to the Red Bull earlier this year for three races [when Isack Hadjar was injured] and did a good job there. And he's delivered really, really well," said Chandhok.

"I get the junior team is a university to prepare drivers for the top team. Today, they are a strong midfield team, have their own identity, own sponsors, own reasons to be competitive and not just be there to train drivers up."

Collins added: "There are two aspects to a feeder team. One is getting very young talent in, getting them ready for the big team but what Liam showed is he can step up into that big team seat and that's important to have someone current that can just step up at any moment.

"I don't really know what he can do and I'm a bit surprised we are talking about it because looking from the outside what's happened at Racing Bulls this year, the points he's scored and the races he's done, he should have done enough, more than enough.

"If anything, we should be discussing Arvid Lindblad's seat because he's the one who hasn't scored as many points. He's had a good year by rookie standards but if you're just looking at the scoresheet, which is what's important to the teams, that's the one you should be discussing - has he done enough against Liam Lawson?"

articles.headline: El Sayed and Stevens feud explodes days before Michigan Senate showdown
keyFacts: Abdul el Sayed and Representative Haley Stevens clashed after Stevens demanded he condemn an advertisement criticizing United States aid to Israel.
This Michigan race matters because el Sayed leads Republican Mike Rogers narrowly in a contest that could determine Senate control.
Politico reported that el Sayed’s campaign subsequently asked Stevens to stay away from all campaign events ahead of the election.
body: Michigan Democratic Senate nominee Abdul el Sayed and Rep. Haley Stevens (D-MI), his former primary opponent, are again sparring over Israel just days before voters decide one of the most closely watched contests of the 2026 midterm elections .

The dispute centers on an advertisement attacking U.S. aid to Israel run by Rebellion PAC, a left-wing group founded by Cenk Uygur — the uncle of el Sayed booster Hasan Piker. The ad blames the high cost of groceries on Israel, which Jewish leaders have condemned as antisemitic.

Stevens asked el Sayed to condemn the advertisement and apologize for his own campaign rhetoric, particularly his suggestion that Israel is responsible for Michigan’s inability to afford schools, healthcare, and childcare.

“If those words are wrong when a Political Action Committee supporting his campaign says them, then they are equally wrong when Abdul says them, and Abdul has said them from the start,” Stevens said in a statement. “I therefore expect him to apologize for those statements as well.”

The request came ahead of what was to be a joint appearance between Stevens, el Sayed, and Rep. Jim Clyburn (D-SC) this weekend at a church in Michigan. El Sayed responded to the request on Friday with a blistering statement of his own accusing Stevens of “relitigating” their primary.

“Our campaign is and has always been focused on addressing the most critical challenges Michiganders are facing: skyrocketing gas prices, unaffordable groceries, and the inability to see a doctor,” el Sayed said. “That focus is why our people-powered campaign defeated a historic $70M in outside spending from big corporations and AlPAC on behalf of Congresswoman Stevens.”
El Sayed argued that it was time to put all of the emphasis on defeating his Republican opponent, former Rep. Mike Rogers.

“So while Congresswoman Stevens seems intent on relitigating a primary that ended three months ago, let’s all focus on the task at hand: that’s beating Mike Rogers, holding Trump accountable, and getting money out of politics, putting money in pockets, and passing Medicare for All,” el Sayed said.
The clash did not stop at the dualing statements, however. According to a Friday Politico report , el Sayed’s campaign has also asked Stevens to stay away from all campaign events.
The Washington Examiner reached out to el Sayed’s campaign for comment.
Rogers was quick to seize on the dispute, saying Stevens was “right” to call out el Sayed in a social media post on Friday evening.

“Representative Haley Stevens is a courageous leader who deserves the respect of every Michigan voter,” he said. “She has conducted herself with nothing but class since the Democratic primary, a primary where a majority of voters did not vote for her party’s nominee.”

Earlier this week, Stevens’s fiancee, Jason Turkish, told the Detroit News he planned to vote for Rogers. Stevens subsequently told CNN that she would vote for el Sayed, describing them as “a household divided,” while calling on his campaign to “shut out the hate and to call it out.”

The Michigan contest is among the key Senate races that could determine control of the chamber. Current polling averages show el Sayed inching ahead of Rogers by only 1 point, according to RealClearPolitics .

articles.headline: Why North Korea's 'elite' hackers are the prime suspect in major Binance hack
keyFacts: Two blockchain analytics firms say a North Korean state-backed group is the likely culprit in a $6.3bn hack of Binance.
Binance co-CEO Richard Teng said investigations uncovered additional points of breach after initially suspecting an engineer's compromised laptop.
A Binance spokesperson said on Friday that about 80% of the stolen assets have been secured while the rest remains unaccounted for.
body: - Published

Two major blockchain analytics firms say they have robust intelligence pointing to a North Korean state-backed group as the likely culprits in the $6.3bn (Â£4.7bn) hack of Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange.
The Lazarus Group, a North Korean hacking unit also known as TraderTraitor, was identified "with high confidence" by TRM Labs, as well as Chainalysis.
This incident is just the latest linked to the country, one of the poorest in the world and where access to the internet is severely restricted.
Experts accuse the government of North Korean leader Kim Jong Un of relying on cybercrime to finance itself, something Pyongyang has long denied.

Though not financial, the nation's most spectacular suspected hack took place in 2014. The target: Sony Pictures, which had made the Hollywood film The Interview. The film involves a plot to assassinate Kim.
The resulting hack exposed thousands of embarrassing emails exchanged among the studio's top executives.
Last year, the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) said North Korea was responsible for the theft of $1.5bn on the Bybit exchange.

In the aftermath of that incident, the agency said TraderTraitor had moved to quickly launder and disperse the stolen assets, converting them to Bitcoin and other digital assets with a goal of eventually turning them into hard currency.
The FBI has broadly accused North Korea of "illicit cybercrime and virtual asset theft activities".

The nation has systematically developed its cyber operations, recruiting the most promising students from universities and channeling them into hacker groups overseen by North Korea's intelligence agency, according to reports.
Some of the cyberwarfare conducted takes place just over the nation's border in China, according to analysis from tech groups.
Much of its hacking activity has centred on monetary gain.
North Korean hackers are also suspected in the theft of $620m worth of cryptocurrency in 2022.

In this most recent heist, North Korean agents are accused of using a special authorisation to turn a Binance hot wallet, which is connected to the internet, into one that moved funds automatically to the attacker.
TRM said it's likely the attacker gained access to Binance's hot wallet signing system as part of the scheme.
Binance has not directly responded to the BBC's queries about the incident's potential links to the area.
The company had initially said it thought an engineer's laptop had been compromised, allowing unauthorised withdrawals, but later said the attack was wider.
"Our subsequent investigation has uncovered additional points of breach," Binance's co-CEO Richard Teng said.
Some 80% of stolen assets have been secured, a Binance spokesperson said on Friday, but the rest remains unaccounted for.
If the accusations are true, the record-making heist shows how powerful suspected North Korean hackers have become â a sign that the tools of the hacking trade have grown sharper.
Experts say the rise of artificial intelligence has also given threat actors new ways to carry out crime, through automation and other means.
In this case, it's plausible that AI was used to infiltrate Binance's systems.
As Chainalysis put it, the attacker used laundering patterns "we have not seen before".

articles.headline: Trump tears into ‘moron’ Robert De Niro, mulls Hollywood tax credits during Daytona Beach rally
keyFacts: President Trump called actor Robert De Niro a moron during a campaign rally in Daytona Beach, Florida.
Trump criticized De Niro and the Academy Awards while discussing potential tax credits for Hollywood.
De Niro has been fundraising for Democrats ahead of the midterm elections, including issuing emails that attacked Trump.
body: WASHINGTON — President Trump revived his feud with Robert De Niro on Friday, saying that the Democrat-backing actor was a “gross” moron who has “something wrong with him” — as he discussed possible tax credits for Hollywood.

Trump veered into attacking the 83-year-old celebrity while mentioning his own former reality TV show “The Apprentice” at a campaign rally in Daytona Beach, Fla., for Republican gubernatorial candidate Byron Donalds.
Trump said his show “beat what used to be a great show, the Academy Awards,” lamented the celebrity fest now “sucks because people get up and use foul language about your favorite president.”
“By the way, is Robert De Niro a moron? He’s a moron,” Trump said — seemingly still fuming over De Niro’s “F–k Trump” speech at the 2018 Tony Awards.

“No, there’s something wrong with him. I used to sort of like him or something, but now I can’t even watch him. He’s like gross. Then he goes into the comedies. He’s no good for comedies. Maybe somebody should tell him, but he’s terrible.”

The “Taxi Driver” star won two Academy Awards — for “The Godfather Part II” and “Raging Bull.” His best-known comedic roles later in his career include his role as a father in “Meet the Parents” in 2000.

It’s unclear what exactly sparked Trump’s ire at De Niro, though the actor has been fundraising for Democrats ahead of the Tuesday midterm elections, including with an email solicitation attacking the “Trump/Epstein class,” connecting the president to the late sex trafficker Jeffrey Epstein.
“Guys that have been saying bad crap about me for years are sitting in my office. ‘Sir, it’s a great honor to be with you, sir,’” Trump told his audience.

“See, the great thing about the Internet is that all you do is you press a button, and it tells you everything they’ve said for the last 20 years,” he added, before impersonating a visiting Hollywood rep pleading, “Sir, I’d like to just say before we begin, I was misquoted when I called you an a–hole.

articles.headline: How To Unlock The Secret Ending In Phantom Blade Zero – True Ending Guide
keyFacts: Unlocking the secret ending in Phantom Blade Zero requires completing specific optional story quests and collecting items before reaching the Mirage Estate point of no return.
Players must finish overarching tasks like Secrets at the Heart of the Lake, acquire Acolyte Masks, and collect Crystal Puppet Eyes to access hidden areas and boss fights.
Completing all required optional missions and defeating the final opponents in Soulrend Cliff allows players to trigger and watch the true ending cutscenes.
body: Are you ready to unlock the secret ending in Phantom Blade Zero ? Every story has its conclusion, including your journey across the Wulin as Soul. That said, there are several requirements that you need to be mindful of, including important quests and points of no return. Our guide discusses every single detail but, because of the topic at hand, you can bet that there will be major spoilers below.

Phantom Blade Zero secret ending - The point of no return and important quests

The Phantom Blade Zero secret ending, also known as the true ending, requires you to complete optional story quests throughout the campaign. It’s pretty much an overarching narrative where you discover the Secrets at the Heart of the Lake, the Herald’s Illusion, and Inanis’s role.
These tasks must be completed before you reach the game’s point of no return: Mirage Estate . Here’s a quick summary:
After completing the main mission in Pangzhen, you learn that you have to go to the Mirage Estate. However, there’s no way to enter via the steps/thoroughfare.
The quest then changes to The Four Serpent Houses . This is when you discern that there’s a hidden passage behind the snake door in the Green Serpent House.

After collecting the items needed to open the doorway, you can continue onward to the Mirage Estate. However, if there are still important quests that you need to tackle, you’ll be warned that you have “unfinished business.”
You can still fast travel to other regions even if you prematurely enter the Mirage Estate. It’s just that the requirements for the true ending might fail, and you don’t want that to happen.
You don't want to enter the Mirage Estate if you still have unfinished story quests in your journal.
Early-game quests and overarching plots

There are early-game quests that you should tackle to unlock the true ending. These include Deep in the Valley , Crimson Manor , Bloodline Awakening/Long Pillars , and Quick Hand Zhang Treasures . (You can check out these guides we’ve linked for more detailed tips.)

Deep in the Valley grants you entry to the lower section of the first region, where you’ll find the Crimson Manor and Long Pillar. Quick Hand Zhang, meanwhile, has you collecting relics in various zones where he has a hideout.
From left to right: Deep in the Valley, Bloodline Awakening, and the Crimson Manor.
Secrets at the Heart of the Lake: The Village of Lu
The Phantom Blade Zero Secrets at the Heart of the Lake is an overarching quest that’s initially started in the Village of Lu.

First, you’ll want to collect the six Firefly’s Memory Flowers scattered all over the village. These allow you to enter an optional area near the Temple of the Blue Fireflies, the settlement with a bunch of friendly puppets.
Jump down the pit and defeat a boss named Dusk, the Puppeteer to receive rewards and trigger a cutscene.
If you defeat an acolyte/scarecrow in the farm fields to the north, you’ll also learn that the objective is part of the quest.
These Memory Flowers give you hints regarding a major quest... that's totally optional.
Exploration and collectibles: The Illusory Pipa, the Acolyte Masks, and the Herald’s Illusion

Certain quests, such as Illusion of Inanis and Sha-Chi-Powered Boat are completed as you continue to explore other regions. For instance, Sha-Chi-Powered Boat leads you to Meigu Lake . As for Whence the Weeping and Pillars of Kunlun, you receive these quests a few hours into the campaign, and you complete them upon clearing the Mountain of Imprisonment .
Other quests also play a major factor:
A good example is the Illusory Pipa , which lets you dispel impenetrable barriers that open up new areas for exploration.
There’s also The Herald’s Illusion , where you seek out the Three-Eyed Puppet’s domains.
Lastly, you should acquire all Acolyte Masks , as these items grant entry to a secret area.
Note: Completing these tasks nets you two Crystal Puppet Eye items (Yin and Yang).
From left to right: The Illusory Pipa, Herald's Illusion, and Acolyte Masks.
Secrets at the Heart of the Lake: The Meigu Lake Discordance and Inanis' Realm

The aforementioned Acolyte Masks are used to shatter the Four Guardians’ Mirror, a mystical location in the frozen lands in northwestern Meigu Lake. Explore the Discordance realm at your leisure and collect more loot. At the very end, you have to defeat the Blizzard Blademaster.

After the Blademaster’s fall, an ominous-looking statue will appear right in front of you. Interact with it and place the two Crystal Puppet Eyes to get transported to the Heart of the Lake. Kill all the cultists to stop their ritual, which then leads you to another encounter with Inanis. This completes the Secrets of the Heart of the Lake.
The two Crystal Puppet Eyes teleport you to the ritual site in the Heart of the Lake.
What happens when you enter the Mirage Estate and Soulrend Cliff

To summarize: If you want to get the secret ending in Phantom Blade Zero, you have to complete all story quests that aren’t tied to the main mission--i.e. those with a purple icon. Once you’ve done all of those, it’s time to enter the Mirage Estate . Doing so causes changes to certain locations, such as the Crimson Forest’s eastern part getting blanketed in snow.
Proceed deeper into the Mirage Estate, fighting enemies, taking out bosses, and picking up all sorts of loot. Along the way, don’t forget to complete the following:
Bloodline Awakening - The fifth and final Long Pillar is in the estate grounds.
Quick Hand’s Request - Quick Hand Zhang has another hideout in the sprawling complex.

Eventually, you’ll acquire the Tiger Cannon, a Phantom Edge that can blow up destructible walls. Use it to reach Soulrend Cliff, the last region in the game. There are still lots of enemies, bosses, and rewards in this area, so just keep forging ahead.

After defeating what’s supposed to be the final boss, it will be followed by yet another encounter. We don’t want to spoil what happens next, but it should be pretty clear that this is your last foe. Once you’ve vanquished your opponent, sit back, relax, and watch the cutscenes.
Discern Inanis' true intentions and proceed further in to the Mirage Estate and Soulrend Cliff.

That does it for our guide on how to get the true ending in Phantom Blade Zero. Keep in mind that you can still fast travel to other locations while you’re in the Mirage Estate and also while in Soulrend Cliff (just prior to the last bell).

You should be able to find other goodies in the game world, such as the Soul Temper materials for your weapons. Also, don’t forget to battle the Three-Faced Puppet as part of the Triple Threat quest . And, if you’re up for even more challenges, you can try 66 Days Mode after beating the game.
Join Soul as he faces numerous threats in the Wulin and be sure to check out more tips in our Phantom Blade Zero guides hub .

articles.headline: Nikita Kucherov trade request: Five potential landing spots for the reigning NHL MVP
keyFacts: Nikita Kucherov told the Tampa Bay Lightning he will not sign a contract extension and has requested a trade, according to Sportsnet.
Kucherov is in the final year of a contract paying $9.5 million per season and is due for a raise next summer.
Potential landing spots for Kucherov include the Montreal Canadiens, Minnesota Wild, Carolina Hurricanes, Utah Mammoth, and Dallas Stars.
body: One of the greatest players in Tampa Bay Lightning history may soon be wearing a different jersey. According to Sportsnet, Nikita Kucherov has told the Lightning he won't sign a contract extension and has requested a trade.

Kucherov, a two-time Stanley Cup champion and two-time Hart Trophy winner as league MVP, is one of the best players of his era. The 33-year-old just passed the legendary Steven Stamkos for the all-time franchise lead in points and has shown no signs of slowing down.

Just last season, Kucherov posted 44 goals and 86 assists en route to his second Hart Trophy win. His underlying numbers were even better with a five-on-five goal differential of plus-38 and an expected goals share of 57.0 percent. Only a select few players can drive play from the wing like Kucherov, and that makes him a unicorn of sorts.

Kucherov is in the final year of a contract that pays him $9.5 million per season, and with the salary cap rising rapidly, he's due for a gargantuan raise next summer. It sounds like Kucherov and the Lightning were too far apart on that number, so the superstar winger has shifted his focuse to a change of scenery.

It's important to note that Kucherov has limited trade protection in the form of a 10-team trade list, but that should be more than enough for the Lightning to find a suitable trade partner. With that in mind, let's take a look at five teams that would be ideal fits for Kucherov as he prepares for the next chapter of his illustrious career.
Montreal Canadiens

Right out of the gate, this is the most natural fit of all the potential landing spots. General manager Kent Hughes has done a superb job of locking down his young core on team-friendly contracts, and as a result, the Canadiens have nearly $30 million in projected cap space for next season. They also have a glaring need in their top two lines, and I'd say the reigning Hart Trophy winner would fill that role quite nicely.

Montreal's moment to strike is now. It's an ascendant team with a great salary cap situtation and assets to spend. It's time to make a splash, and this would be a tsunami. Just imagine Kucherov on a power play unit with Nick Suzuki, Cole Caufield, Lane Hutson and Ivan Demidov. Kucherov would also be coached by former Lightning teammate Martin St. Louis, so a rapport would already exist between player and coach. I expect the Canadiens to do everything in their power to land Kucherov.
Minnesota Wild

We already know the Wild are big-game hunting at forward because they've been heavily linked to former Detroit Red Wings captain Dylan Larkin. If I were advising general manager Bill Guerin -- and I'm certainly not -- I would recommend Minnesota package whatever assets it has offered Detroit and redirect them to Tampa Bay. No, Kucherov is not a center, and that's the Wild's biggest need.

However, Kucherov is a rare breed of winger in that he can drive play better than most first-line centers from the wing. Put him on a line with Kirill Kaprizov, and the only time opponents will touch the puck is when they're pulling out of the net.

With Quinn Hughes also on an expiring contract, acquiring Kucherov would be a risky move for the Wild. What if they give up premium assets only to lose Kucherov and Hughes next summer? I don't think fear can dictate Minnesota's decisions. The team has a top-two defenseman in the world on its roster right now, and it has the opportunity to acquire a top-five forward. Worry about next summer when the time comes. Go all in to win the Cup while you have a chance.
Carolina Hurricanes

It was no secret that the Hurricanes were in on the Connor Hellebuyck sweepstakes but just missed out. So, if they can't get better at preventing goals, why not get much better at scoring them? Carolina doesn't exactly need any help offensively, but adding Kucherov would go a long way to helping the team repeat as Stanley Cup champions. Besides, Kucherov would provide another level of playmaking and finishing that the Canes don't currently have on their roster.

Carolina has a good chunk of cap space available already, and it wouldn't need to shed much in order to make room for Kucherov. The Canes also have some enticing young players on their roster that might appeal to the Bolts, and they have three first-round picks over the next two drafts. Why not take a shot at landing a superstar winger?
Utah Mammoth

Similar to the Hurricanes, the Mammoth were in the mix to acquire Hellebucyk, and for good reason. The goaltending tandem of Karel Vejmelka and Sebastian Cossa has not been good, so Utah may have to outscore its problems until one of the goalies finds a groove. Offense may be the best defense for the Mammoth -- and if that's the case -- then Kucherov should be in the mix for the Norris Trophy. There is a great young core of forwards in Salt Lake City, and I think Kucherov would be a perfect fit alongside Logan Cooley, who is emerging as a franchise center.

Utah also has plenty of draft capital with which to work, and it's projected for just over $25 million in salary cap space next season. The Mammoth don't have any major pending free agents on their cap sheet, so they're a suitor capable of signing Kucherov to a long-term extension.
Dallas Stars

Allow me to get a little bold on the fifth and final destination. The Stars have already failed to sign 27-year-old winger Jason Robertson to a long-term extension once. The two sides agreed to a one-year deal worth $12 million prior to the season, but Robertson's future with the team is still very much in doubt. What if Dallas and Tampa Bay executed a true "hockey trade" -- one player for one player?

Dallas would get the better player in Kucherov, but there are no guarantees regarding an extension. The Stars are in win-now mode, and Kucherov could help them get over the Cup hump immediately. Tampa Bay would get a younger player in Robertson, and although he doesn't have the elite playmaking ability of Kucherov, he's still an exceptionally talented scorer. Perhaps the Bolts could get him to join the team's core and sign a multi-year contract. This deal could work for both sides.
